Reviewed `receipt-lines` against `main` at `a6c40d4`. **I’d fix these before merging:**

1. **[P1] Printed amounts are 100× too large** — `receipt/render.py:2`  
   `format_money()` formats integer cents directly as dollars: `format_money(1299)` returns `$1299.00`, not `$12.99`. Two coffees at 450 cents print as `$900.00` instead of `$9.00`. Convert cents to dollars before formatting. Add an assertion against a literal expected value—the current rendering test uses the same broken formatter to calculate its expectation, so it passes.

2. **[P2] The printed renderer doesn’t use the right-alignment helper** — `receipt/render.py:7`  
   `render_line()` pads the name to 20 characters, then appends the amount. Amounts of different lengths therefore end in different columns rather than at the 32-character right edge. The new `align()` helper is only exercised by its test, not the renderer. Wire alignment into the rendering path and test differing amount widths. Also define wrapping or truncation for long labels: a name like `Extra-large coffee with oat milk` currently produces a 40-character line, exceeding `WIDTH = 32`.

All **3 existing tests pass**, but they don’t catch these issues. No files changed.
